faqs.q: What's the age range on your trips?
faqs.a: Most of the group will be somewhere between 18 and 35, and our trips are open to anyone up to 45. Backpacker trips are just for 18–29s. If you're over 45 and you've travelled with us before, drop the team a line at info@trutravels.com and we'll see what we can do.

faqs.q: What's the age mix on a specific trip like Thailand Island Hopper or Greece?
faqs.a: Every group is a mix, but on most Classic trips you'll find people in their 20s and early 30s, with Greece and Europe by Rail skewing 18–30. Backpacker trips are 18–29 only. Whatever your age, you'll be with people who said yes to the same thing you did.

faqs.q: Do many people travel solo?
faqs.a: Most do. Around 65% of TruTravellers arrive on their own, so the person next to you at the welcome dinner is probably in the same boat. You'll be chatting in the group WhatsApp before you fly, and by day two the group chat won't shut up.

faqs.q: I've never travelled solo before and I'm nervous. Is this for me?
faqs.a: You don't have to be fearless. You just have to go. Nearly everyone on a Tru trip came alone, so nobody's the odd one out. You'll share a room with another solo traveller of the same gender, your Local Legend is with you from the first evening, and the group is talking on WhatsApp before you've even packed. Nervous is normal. It usually lasts until about the second drink on night one.

faqs.q: Is it safe for a solo female traveller?
faqs.a: Yes. Travelling with a small group and a Local Legend who calls the place home is about the safest way to see the world on your own. Transport, accommodation and activities are sorted, and there's always someone who knows the ground. If you'd rather travel with an all-female group, we run community departures with partners like Gals Who Travel.

faqs.q: How many people are on each trip?
faqs.a: Between 10 and 20, depending on the trip. Small enough that nobody sits on the edge of the group, big enough that you'll find your people. Groups do fill up, so if a date is calling you, don't sit on it.

faqs.q: Can I join if I'm not from the UK?
faqs.a: Of course. Our groups come from all over the world, and that mix is half the fun. Prices show in GBP, AUD, CAD, EUR and USD.

faqs.q: Are your trips all about partying?
faqs.a: No. Evenings are a big part of a Tru trip, but they're yours. Some nights the group heads out for drinks; others it's a night market, a sunset, a card game that gets out of hand. Your Local Legend always has a non-drinking option, and nothing in the evening is compulsory.

faqs.q: Are your trips LGBTQ+ friendly?
faqs.a: Yes. Everyone is welcome on a Tru trip, and we also run community departures with LGBTQ+ partners. Some destinations are especially open: Thailand is one of the most LGBTQ+ friendly countries in Asia, and Vietnam's big cities are relaxed and welcoming.

faqs.q: What are Life Moments?
faqs.a: A way to find your trip by where you are in life rather than just where you want to go. Gap Year, Just Left Uni, Looking To Challenge Myself, Solo Soul Searcher, Turning 30 and Work Break Recharge each pull together the trips that fit that chapter. Different stage of life, different kind of trip.

faqs.q: What's a good first trip?
faqs.a: Thailand Island Hopper, Bali Experience and Thailand Experience are the classic first-timers: easy to get to, friendly, and full of people doing exactly what you're doing. The Explore page has a 'Perfect First Trips' shelf, or answer a few questions on Inspire Me and we'll match you.

faqs.q: Is everything included?
faqs.a: Everything that matters for getting around and getting stuck in: all your accommodation, all transport between destinations, every activity on the itinerary, airport pickup on arrival day, some meals (welcome and farewell dinners always) and your Local Legend. What's not included: international flights, travel insurance and most day-to-day meals, because you'll want to find your own spots.

faqs.q: What's a Tru trip actually like?
faqs.a: Land somewhere new knowing nobody. Leave a couple of weeks later with a camera roll full of ridiculous moments, a group chat that won't shut up, and at least one thing you never thought you'd be brave enough to try. Underneath that there's an itinerary, a Local Legend and all the logistics handled, so you can just turn up and say yes.

faqs.q: What does 'Leave Ordinary Behind' mean?
faqs.a: It's the belief underneath everything we do. Not escaping your life, expanding it. Travel gives you permission to say yes more, meet people you'd never normally meet, try things that scare you a little and come home with more confidence, connection and possibility than you left with. The destination is the setting. What happens to you is the story.

faqs.q: What are the Tru Experience Types?
faqs.a: Every Tru trip is intentionally designed around five kinds of moment. Local Lens: see the place through the people who live there. Rise Up: step past comfortable and find out what you're capable of. Bucket List: the iconic moments you pictured before you booked. Tru-ly Unique: experiences made possible through our own relationships and ideas, just for the Tru community. Unplugged: phone away, slow down, be there. On each trip page you can filter the itinerary by type to see how the trip delivers them.

faqs.q: What's a Local Lens experience?
faqs.a: Seeing a destination through someone who calls it home. Cooking with a family in Ubud, wandering Hoi An with a local artisan, a hill-tribe homestay in the Atlas or northern Thailand. It's where a place stops feeling foreign and starts feeling personal.

faqs.q: What's a Rise Up experience?
faqs.a: The moment you step past comfortable. A 3am alarm for the Mount Batur sunrise, the climb up Sigiriya Rock, a first surf lesson, the Inca Trail. Challenging in a supportive way, never macho. You arrive unsure. You leave stronger.

faqs.q: What's a Bucket List experience?
faqs.a: The ones you've seen in photos and imagined being in: sunrise at Angkor Wat, an overnight boat on Ha Long Bay, Maya Bay, Komodo dragons, the Taj Mahal at first light. The reason you started looking at the trip in the first place.

faqs.q: What's a Tru-ly Unique experience?
faqs.a: Something you can only do with us, made possible by our relationships and our own ideas. One night where Bottle Beach is ours, with a fire show on the sand. A cooking class in Wayan's family home in Ubud. Moyo Island, where only around 50 people a day are allowed. Not scarcity for its own sake, just moments that feel distinctively Tru.

faqs.q: What's an Unplugged experience?
faqs.a: The quiet bit. Floating bungalows on a lake in Khao Sok with no Wi-Fi. A silent sunrise on a Sri Lankan beach. A hammock afternoon in Costa Rica. Not every extraordinary moment needs adrenaline; sometimes it's a cup of tea in the jungle and a conversation that runs long after dinner.

faqs.q: Why doesn't every trip show all five Experience Types?
faqs.a: Because we only tag a moment when the trip genuinely delivers it. Some trips lean harder into one type than another, which is exactly why you can search by the kind of experiences you want, not just the country. A Thailand Island Hopper leans Bucket List and Unplugged; a Morocco trip leans Local Lens.

faqs.q: What happened to TruExclusives?
faqs.a: They've evolved into Tru-ly Unique experiences. Same idea, a bigger ambition: moments created for the Tru community through our own access, partnerships and ideas, explained by why they feel special rather than shouted as 'exclusive'.

faqs.q: Who is my guide?
faqs.a: A Local Legend. Someone who feels more like a mate who happens to know the way. Born where they guide (or as good as), with you day and evening, not just nine to five. They know which street-food stall to order from, the story behind the place you're standing, and when the group needs a push, a laugh or a moment to slow down.

faqs.q: What happened to Tru Leaders?
faqs.a: Same people, bigger role. Our guides have been Travel Ninjas and Tru Leaders over the years; from 2026 they're Local Legends. It's not a cosmetic rename. They're trained around the five Experience Types and asked to turn every stop into a story, not just tick off the itinerary.

faqs.q: What are the different travel styles?
faqs.a: Classic: our signature trip, big on inclusions, a great mix of places to stay, open to 18–45. Backpacker: maximum adventure, minimum cost, hostels and street food, exclusively for 18–29s. Flashpacker: all the adventure with an upgrade, boutique stays and a few extra touches. Multi Country: cross borders and pack more in. Limited Edition: trips that run only a handful of times around a festival or an event. When they're gone, they're gone.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Classic and Backpacker?
faqs.a: Classic trips are packed with inclusions and stay in hotels, homestays, beach huts and the odd boat, twin-share. Backpacker trips cost less, stay in hand-picked hostels (usually dorms), leave more free time and are just for 18–29s. Same destinations, different budget and vibe.

faqs.q: What's a Flashpacker trip?
faqs.a: All the adventure with an upgrade. Think boutique hotels, a few premium experiences and the extra touches that make a day feel special. For people who like comfort with their chaos.

faqs.q: Are departures guaranteed?
faqs.a: Yes. Every trip runs, so once you've booked you can lock in flights with total peace of mind.

faqs.q: Is TruTravels financially protected?
faqs.a: Yes. We're ABTA members (Y6506) and ATOL protected, so your booking is fully financially protected under the Package Travel Regulations. If anything ever happened to us, your trip would still go ahead or you'd get your money back.

faqs.q: Do you run all-female or community-only departures?
faqs.a: Yes. Alongside our main departures we run community trips with partners like Gals Who Travel, Females Flying Solo and Influence & Inspire. Same itinerary and Local Legend, but the departure is only open to that community, booked through the partner's page.

faqs.q: Can I host my own trip for my community?
faqs.a: Yes. If you've got a community, online or in person, you can host a Tru trip for them. You pitch the idea, we build the itinerary, price it, assign a Local Legend and set dates. You promote it with a dedicated page and travel as part of the group while the Local Legend runs the logistics. You earn commission on bookings. No follower count required, just an engaged community and a destination in mind. Hosts and travellers need to be 18+.

faqs.q: Do you have an affiliate programme?
faqs.a: Yes. Tru Affiliates get a personal landing page, trackable links for each trip, ready-made post templates and commission on every completed booking (minimum 5%, with boosts for volume and campaigns). There's no minimum following; engagement matters more than numbers. Apply on the Affiliates page.

faqs.q: I'm a travel agent. How do I sell Tru trips?
faqs.a: Register your agency on the Agent Registration page (it registers the agency, not an individual). Once approved you'll get access to Sherpa, our agent platform, and can give individual agents at your firm their own logins. Already registered? Log in to Sherpa.

faqs.q: The date I want is sold out. How does the waitlist work?
faqs.a: Spots open up when plans change, and they go to the waitlist first. Give us your name and email and we'll add you for that date. If a place frees up you'll get a priority booking link by email that holds the spot for 24 hours before it moves to the next person, so keep an eye on your inbox.

faqs.q: When will new departure dates be released?
faqs.a: As soon as our local teams have locked in transport and places to stay. Leave your email and we'll message you the second new dates for that trip go live.

faqs.q: Can I check if there are still places on a specific date?
faqs.a: Live availability is under Check Dates on each trip page. 'Last places' means it's nearly full, so grab it with a £200 deposit. Sold out? Join the waitlist and we'll tell you the moment a spot opens.

faqs.q: How do I hear about Limited Edition trips like Rio Carnival?
faqs.a: Limited Edition trips run a handful of times and sell fast. Sign up on the homepage banner or the trip page and you'll be first in line when dates and prices go live.

faqs.q: Can I get a private room?
faqs.a: Most trips are twin-share with another traveller of the same gender, and private room upgrades are available on selected trips and legs. Tell us the trip and date you're looking at and we'll check what's possible.

faqs.q: My friend and I are booking separately. Can we share a room?
faqs.a: Yes. As long as you're on the same departure date, send us both booking references and we'll link your bookings so the team on the ground rooms you together. Same for cabins on overnight trains.

faqs.q: Can a group of us travel together?
faqs.a: Definitely. Book the same departure and tell us you're together so we can room you as a group. Bigger group, or a community you'd like to bring? Look at Host A Trip, or email info@trutravels.com.

faqs.q: Can I combine two trips back-to-back?
faqs.a: Yes. Multi Country trips like Cambodia & Vietnam Explorer or Total Thailand are built as one journey with everything included. You can also bundle any two or more trips for 5% off. Bundles don't include flights between trips, so leave a day or two between the end of one and the start of the next for the flight and any visa admin.

faqs.q: If I book more than one trip, is transport between them included?
faqs.a: For bundles, no, but we'll help you plan the best way between them. Pre-built Multi Country trips do include all transport within the itinerary, including the border crossing.

faqs.q: Does Bali & Beyond include Komodo?
faqs.a: Yes. The 18-day Bali & Beyond takes in Bali, the Gilis, Lombok, Sumbawa and three days on our own liveaboard boat through the Komodo islands, ending in Labuan Bajo. Just want the boat and the dragons? That's the 9-day Komodo Island Hopper.

faqs.q: Does Total Thailand cover both the north and the islands?
faqs.a: Yes. 27 days, Bangkok to Phuket: Kanchanaburi, Ayutthaya, Chiang Mai, the hill-tribe homestay, Pai, Khao Sok, Koh Phangan, Koh Tao and Phi Phi in one seamless trip.

faqs.q: Can I connect Europe by Rail with the Greece Island Hopper?
faqs.a: Yes. The rail trip ends in Milan and Greece starts in Athens, so you'll need a short budget flight between them. Leave a couple of days in Athens before the islands.
faqs.applies: Europe by Rail / Greece Island Hopper

faqs.q: Are internal flights included on the Philippines trips?
faqs.a: Yes. Every internal flight on the itinerary is included, with a 20kg checked bag each time. Philippines West includes Manila to Puerto Princesa; Philippines Island Hopper includes three internal flights. The one you book yourself is the flight back to Manila at the end, from Coron or Caticlan.

faqs.q: Are ferries between the Thai islands included?
faqs.a: Yes. All transport on the itinerary is in: the private van, the overnight sleeper train south and the ferries between Koh Phangan, Koh Tao and Phi Phi. No domestic flights to book.

faqs.q: Is the Ha Long Bay cruise included on Vietnam Explorer?
faqs.a: Yes. The overnight boat on Ha Long Bay, the flight from Ho Chi Minh City to Hoi An and the overnight train are all included.

faqs.q: Is the Ella train and the safari included on Sri Lanka Uncovered?
faqs.a: Yes. The train to Ella (seven hours of tea plantations and hanging out of the door), the Udawalawe safari, Sigiriya Rock and the tea plantation visit are all part of the trip.

faqs.q: Are the bullet trains included on Legend of Japan?
faqs.a: Yes. Shinkansen between cities and local transport (metro, bus, trains) are all included on the 12-day Legend of Japan, Tokyo to Osaka.

faqs.q: Are ziplining and the hot springs included on Costa Rica Adventure?
faqs.a: Yes. Cloud-forest ziplining in Monteverde, the volcanic hot springs in La Fortuna, a night wildlife walk and a rural homestay are all part of the 10 days from San José to Santa Teresa.

faqs.q: Is the Inca Trail permit and Machu Picchu included on Peru Inca Adventure?
faqs.a: Yes. Your Inca Trail permit, the one-day trek, the guided Machu Picchu visit with transport back and the Rainbow Mountain trek are all included. Permits sell out months ahead, so an early deposit is the way to lock yours in.

faqs.q: Which Greek islands does the Greece Island Hopper visit?
faqs.a: Athens, Mykonos, Ios and Santorini, ferries included, starting in Athens and ending in Santorini.

faqs.q: Which cities does Europe by Rail (Budapest to Milan) visit?
faqs.a: Budapest, Vienna, Ljubljana, Lake Bled, Venice and Milan over 11 days. All trains between cities are included and the group's seats are booked together wherever the operators allow.

faqs.q: Is Australia East Coast available?
faqs.a: It's being reimagined and comes back at the end of 2026. Leave your email and we'll tell you the moment dates go live.

faqs.q: What's the Komodo liveaboard boat like?
faqs.a: Three days and two nights on our own boat. Bunk cabins for four with air-con, two western toilets, a traditional shower, free drinking water and three deck areas for lounging. You sail through the first night and wake up near Pink Beach on the second. No signal, all stars.
faqs.applies: Komodo Island Hopper / Bali & Beyond / Total Indonesia

faqs.q: What's the hill-tribe homestay like on Northern Thailand Adventure?
faqs.a: A Local Lens night you'll talk about for years. You trek through the jungle (three to four hours, moderate, plenty of stops) to a hill-tribe village, sleep in a shared homestay, eat what the family cooks and go bamboo rafting in the morning. No high fitness level needed, just a bit of a challenge.

faqs.q: What if the Full Moon Party date moves?
faqs.a: The party falls on a specific date each month, so the days around it can shuffle. You won't miss it, or anything else on the itinerary.

faqs.q: Is the elephant sanctuary ethical?
faqs.a: Yes. On our Thailand trips we visit a Planeterra-partnered sanctuary where the elephants are rehabilitated, not ridden. No riding, no chains, just elephants being elephants. Animal welfare is close to our hearts; we also support Horses of Gili, a locally led non-profit for the working horses on Gili T.

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be?
faqs.a: Normal fitness is plenty, and almost everything is optional. A few Rise Up moments are worth knowing about: the one-day Inca Trail in Peru (12km at altitude), the jungle trek to the hill-tribe homestay in northern Thailand (three to four hours), the Sigiriya Rock climb in Sri Lanka and the 650 steps up El Peñol in Colombia. Bali is beaches, a surf lesson and easy walks at your own pace.

faqs.q: How hard is the Inca Trail on the Peru trip?
faqs.a: It's the one-day Inca Trail: around 12km with some steep steps at altitude, topping out near 2,700m. You don't need to be a runner, just comfortable walking uphill. A few long walks in the months before help. You get a full day in Cusco to acclimatise first, and there's coca tea on hand. Bring good vibes and you'll make it.

faqs.q: Is there a weight limit for ziplining?
faqs.a: On our Thailand trips the zipline has a limit of 115kg (253 lbs). If it's not for you, sit it out; your Local Legend will sort something else.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Bali?
faqs.a: It's warm all year. April to October is dry and sunny; November to March brings quick tropical showers that clear fast.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Thailand?
faqs.a: November to March is the sweet spot: cooler, drier, perfect for temples, islands and trekking. March to May is hot but quieter. June to October is monsoon season, but showers are short and tropical and there's still plenty of beach time.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit the Philippines?
faqs.a: November to May, the dry season, is ideal for island hopping, diving and beach life. Typhoon season runs June to October, but trips still run.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Vietnam?
faqs.a: It depends where you are: the north (Hanoi, Ha Long Bay) is best October to April, central Vietnam (Hoi An, Hue) February to August, the south November to April. For the whole country, March–April or September–December work well.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Costa Rica?
faqs.a: December to April is the dry season. May to November is the green season: lush rainforest, fewer people and afternoon showers.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Morocco?
faqs.a: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November): warm but comfortable for cities, desert and mountains. Summer can be extreme in the Sahara, and winter can bring snow to the Atlas.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: December to March for the south and west coasts, where our trip spends most of its time. The east coast peaks April to September. Pack a light rain jacket whenever you go.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Japan?
faqs.a: Spring (March–May) for cherry blossom and autumn (September–November) for the colours. Summer is hot and humid but full of festivals.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Greece?
faqs.a: May, June and September: warm sea, great weather and fewer crowds than peak summer.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Peru?
faqs.a: May to October, the dry season, with clear skies and the Inca Trail at its best. Nights are cold year-round, so pack layers.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit India?
faqs.a: October to March: cooler and mostly dry. Summer is extremely hot and monsoon runs June to September.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Cambodia?
faqs.a: November to April, the dry season, for temples and cities. May to October brings afternoon rain, greener landscapes and fewer crowds.

faqs.q: Do I need an account to book?
faqs.a: No, you can browse and book without one. A free account is worth having though: it saves trips you're eyeing up, unlocks member deals, tracks your VIP days and holds your bookings and profile in one place. One free account unlocks everything. No catch.

faqs.q: How do deals work?
faqs.a: Sale departures, last-minute discounts and early-bird prices, all shown on the Deals page and on each trip's departure list as a percentage off the full price. Gone when they're gone. Members get extra deals through their account, and you can filter deals by departure timing, price and saving.

faqs.q: Do you do student discounts?
faqs.a: Yes, through Student Beans. Verified students can grab a discount; find it under Essentials.

faqs.q: What is the VIP Programme?
faqs.a: The more you travel, the more you earn. Every day on a Tru trip counts, your status never expires, and you level up automatically. Game-Changer (30+ days): 5% off full-price trips, £50 travel credit a year, early access to flash sales. Icon (50+): 10% off, £100 credit, free airport transfer on every trip. Legend (100+): 15% off, £200 credit, a free pre-night on every trip, priority room upgrades, an invite to the annual Legend meetup. MVP (365+): 20% off, £500 credit, complimentary upgrades, an annual trip for two on us and a personal travel concierge. Track it all on your dashboard.

faqs.q: Where can I read reviews?
faqs.a: Google (4.8, 1,300+ reviews), Trustpilot (4.9, 3,600+) and TourRadar (4.9, 17,000+), plus real reviews on every trip page. Don't just take our word for it.

faqs.q: Do I need travel insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. It's a condition of booking and we'll check it on day one. Your policy needs to cover the whole trip: emergency medical and repatriation, cancellation and curtailment, lost or stolen gear, 24/7 assistance and the activities you'll be doing (trekking, snorkelling, surfing and so on). World Nomads covers 150+ adventure activities and is a good place to start, though we don't represent them and it's not a recommendation to buy.

faqs.q: Does it matter which insurer I use?
faqs.a: No, any reputable insurer is fine if the policy covers your whole trip and your activities. Don't just pick the cheapest; look for one that pays the hospital directly rather than making you pay up front and claim back.

faqs.q: Are flights included?
faqs.a: No. You book your own flights to the start city and home from the end city (Skyscanner and Kayak are good for comparing). Send us the details once you're sorted.

faqs.q: Do I need to book flights before I book the trip?
faqs.a: No. Lock in your spot first (departures are guaranteed), then sort flights whenever works for you. Send us the details once you have them; if we haven't got them 14 days before the trip we'll chase you.

faqs.q: What day should I arrive?
faqs.a: Day 1 of the trip, any time. There's nothing scheduled until the evening welcome dinner, which is where the group first meets. Arrive the day before if you'd like a night's sleep first; we can arrange a pre-night.

faqs.q: What day should I book my flight home?
faqs.a: The last day is checkout day with no activities, but on some trips there's travel that morning, so book a later flight or fly the following day. Several trips end in a different city from where they start, so check the end city on your trip page.

faqs.q: Which airport do I fly into?
faqs.a: The start city on your trip page. For example: Bali Experience is Denpasar (DPS); Thailand trips are Bangkok (BKK or DMK); Philippines is Manila (MNL); Morocco Uncovered is Marrakech (RAK); Greece is Athens (ATH); Legend of Japan is Tokyo (HND or NRT); Vietnam Explorer is Ho Chi Minh City; Peru is Cusco; India is Delhi (DEL); Colombia is Medellín (MDE); Brazil Experience is Rio (GIG). Each trip page has a 'which airport' FAQ.

faqs.q: Two of us are on different flights. Can we share the airport pickup?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. If both flights land on day 1 within the standard pickup window, send us both flight numbers and we'll align your pickup so you arrive at the hotel together.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa?
faqs.a: Depends on your passport and where you're going. Use the Visa Checker on our Visas & Passports page (powered by Sherpa) for a quick answer, then confirm with your government's official travel advice and apply through official channels. Once you've booked we send visa guidance for your trip.

faqs.q: How long does my passport need to be valid?
faqs.a: Most destinations want at least six months' validity from the day you enter, and some want blank pages. Renewing? We can hold your booking on your current passport number and update it later.

faqs.q: My passport is being renewed. Can I still book, or keep my Inca Trail permit?
faqs.a: Yes. We lock in your booking (and your Inca Trail permit on the Peru trip) with your current passport number. When the new one arrives, email us a photo of the main page and we'll update everything.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.a: Most nationalities get 30–60 days visa-free on arrival. Everyone completes Thailand's Digital Arrival Card online within three days before landing and shows the confirmation at immigration. Check the rules for your passport.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Indonesia / Bali?
faqs.a: Most visitors need a 30-day Visa on Arrival (at the main airports) or an e-Visa applied for online beforehand, plus the All-Indonesia Arrival Card before you land. Check the rules for your passport.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for the Philippines?
faqs.a: Most nationalities get visa-free entry on arrival. One thing that catches people out: you need proof of an onward ticket leaving the Philippines within 30 days, or the airline may not let you board.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Vietnam?
faqs.a: Most visitors need an e-visa, applied for online before travel; some passports (UK included) get visa-free short stays. Rules change often, so check and apply early. Combining Thailand and Vietnam? Leave a day or two between trips for the e-visa and the flight.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Cambodia?
faqs.a: Most travellers do. The e-Visa is the easiest way to sort it before you fly; visa on arrival works at major airports and border crossings too. On Cambodia & Vietnam Explorer you cross into Vietnam by land at Moc Bai with the group.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Sri Lanka?
faqs.a: Most nationalities need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), applied for online before you arrive. Fees vary by passport.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for India?
faqs.a: Most travellers do. The e-Visa is the simplest route, applied for online before departure (applications usually open about 30 days before arrival).

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Morocco?
faqs.a: Many nationalities enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Your passport needs six months' validity.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Japan?
faqs.a: Many nationalities visit visa-free for up to 90 days. Check for your passport.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Peru?
faqs.a: Most don't. UK, EU, US, Canadian, Australian and New Zealand passports get 180 days on arrival. Six months' passport validity needed.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Costa Rica?
faqs.a: Most travellers get 90 days visa-free, but you'll need proof of onward travel.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Greece or Europe by Rail?
faqs.a: EU passports, nothing needed. UK and many other nationalities get 90 days visa-free in the Schengen Area. Once ETIAS is live, non-EU travellers will need that authorisation too (around €7, sorted at least four days before travel).

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for China?
faqs.a: Lots of nationalities can now visit China visa-free for short stays, but check for yours. Once booked we send visa guidance, and we'll need your passport details about 60 days before departure so the bullet-train seats can be reserved.

faqs.q: Do I need any vaccinations?
faqs.a: For most of our destinations, nothing specific, but keep tetanus up to date and check with your doctor or a travel clinic. Your country's official travel-health guidance (NHS Fit for Travel in the UK) has destination-specific advice. We can't give medical advice.

faqs.q: Can I drink the tap water?
faqs.a: Mostly no: stick to bottled or filtered water, and ice in bigger hotels and restaurants is usually fine. Japan is the exception, where tap water is generally safe.

faqs.q: What about altitude on the Peru trip?
faqs.a: Cusco sits high, so you get a full day there to acclimatise before the trek, and the hotels have coca tea on hand. Take day one slowly, drink lots of water and go steady.

faqs.q: What if I have an allergy or dietary requirement?
faqs.a: Tell us when you book so your Local Legend knows, and we'll brief cooking classes and homestays too. Carrying allergy cards in the local language is a smart move for restaurants. Vegetarian and vegan options are easy in most of our destinations, Thailand especially.

faqs.q: How much spending money should I take?
faqs.a: Everyone's different, but around £150–£250 a week goes a long way in Asia for food, drinks and shopping, since accommodation, transport and activities are covered. In Thailand that's roughly £15–25 a day. Budget more for Europe, Japan and Latin America.

faqs.q: How should I carry my money?
faqs.a: A travel card with good rates (Monzo, Revolut or similar) and cash from local ATMs. ATMs are easy to find everywhere we go, though most charge a fee per withdrawal, so take out a bit more, less often. Cash is still king at markets and small stalls. Your Local Legend knows the cheapest ATMs.

faqs.q: Can I get Moroccan dirham or Indian rupees before I go?
faqs.a: No. Both are closed currencies, so you can't buy them at home. Withdraw from an ATM on arrival (plenty in Marrakech and Delhi) or exchange cash in-country.

faqs.q: What's the tipping culture, and is there a group kitty?
faqs.a: In Morocco and India tipping is a big part of hospitality, so your Local Legend may suggest an optional group kitty on day one to cover drivers and local staff without the awkwardness. Tipping your Local Legend is entirely up to you.

faqs.q: Backpack or suitcase?
faqs.a: Backpack. Every time. Wheels don't work on beaches, boat decks or overhead train racks. If it's your first time with a backpack, you won't go back.

faqs.q: Are there luggage weight limits?
faqs.a: On trips with internal flights (Philippines, Vietnam, Colombia) the included flights allow roughly 20–23kg checked plus a small carry-on, so pack under 20kg to be safe. Ferries are relaxed. On Europe by Rail there's no limit, but you need to lift your bag into the overhead rack. Private-van trips like Morocco have no limit, though a backpack is still the move.

faqs.q: What should I pack for the Sahara night on Morocco Uncovered?
faqs.a: A small overnight bag with essentials and a change of clothes; your main bag stays in the van. Desert nights get cold, even in summer, so bring warm layers for the evening and the sunrise, plus sunglasses and a scarf for the sand.

faqs.q: What should I pack for the Peru trek?
faqs.a: Layers, because Peru nights are cold all year and the trek climbs. Walking shoes you've already broken in, a light waterproof, sun protection and a daypack.

faqs.q: Is there a packing list?
faqs.a: Yes. Your pre-departure pack has a day-by-day packing list, a climate guide and local transport tips for your trip. It lands about two weeks before you go and lives in your account.

faqs.q: How do I stay connected on the trip?
faqs.a: Grab an eSIM before you fly so you're online the moment you land. We recommend Airalo (code TRUTRAVELS15 for 15% off). Every hotel and most cafés have Wi-Fi. A couple of Unplugged stops, like the floating bungalows in Khao Sok, have no signal on purpose.

faqs.q: When will I hear from my Local Legend?
faqs.a: About a week before departure you'll get a welcome message from your Local Legend introducing themselves, confirming day 1 and adding you to the group WhatsApp. That's when the trip really starts: by the time you land, you'll already know a few names.

faqs.q: Can I find out who else is in my group?
faqs.a: You'll meet everyone in the WhatsApp group your Local Legend sets up about a week before you go. Until then, the TruTravellers Facebook group is full of past and future travellers.

faqs.q: Are airport transfers included?
faqs.a: Airport pickup on arrival day is included. Need another transfer, say a different day or the airport at the end? Add it in your account or ask the team at info@trutravels.com at least 7 days before you travel. Late transfer bookings can't be accepted.

faqs.q: Can I book a pre-night before the trip starts?
faqs.a: Yes. We can arrange extra nights at the start hotel so you don't have to move rooms. Send us the dates and we'll come back with rates. Pre-nights aren't included in the trip price (Legend and MVP VIPs get one free).

faqs.q: What happens after I book?
faqs.a: You'll get a confirmation email and access to your account, where you can pay your balance, add transfers and update your details. Around two weeks out your pre-departure pack arrives, and a week out your Local Legend adds you to the group WhatsApp. From the moment you book, you're in.

faqs.q: I booked before the site changed. Will my trip be different?
faqs.a: Same trip, same places, same Local Legend. What's evolved is how we design and talk about the moments on it: your Local Legend will introduce the five Experience Types on your welcome night, and we're adding Unplugged moments to itineraries over time. Everything you booked is still there.

faqs.q: What does a Local Legend actually do?
faqs.a: Runs the trip, and then some. They handle the logistics so you don't have to, and they're with you day and evening. But the real job is noticing the opportunity inside the itinerary: the story on the bus, the detour worth taking, the introduction, the encouragement before you try something new. The question isn't 'did the activity happen', it's 'what will you remember about how it happened'.

faqs.q: Will my Local Legend talk about the Experience Types on the trip?
faqs.a: Yes, lightly. On the welcome night they'll explain the five types you'll hear about over the trip, and they'll name a moment as Local Lens or Rise Up when it adds meaning. It's never a branded presentation; the experience comes first, the label just helps you see why the moment matters.

faqs.q: What accommodation do we stay in?
faqs.a: Hotels, hostels, homestays, beach huts, floating bungalows, even boats: we mix it up to fit the destination, comfortable where it counts and local and characterful everywhere else. Mostly twin-share rooms with a same-sex roommate, occasionally a triple or a dorm just for our group. You'll always have a clean bed, hot water and somewhere to dump your bag. Exact properties can change, but the standard doesn't.

faqs.q: Who will I share with?
faqs.a: Another traveller of the same gender and a similar age, and they're almost always solo too. If you click with someone on the trip, your Local Legend can usually room you together on request.

faqs.q: What are the overnight trains like?
faqs.a: Thailand, Vietnam and India trips include sleeper trains: air-conditioned berths in shared compartments, usually four to six people. Falling asleep to the rhythm of the rails and waking up somewhere new is one of the moments people talk about afterwards. Friends on linked bookings share a cabin where possible.

faqs.q: What's the desert camp like on Morocco Uncovered?
faqs.a: One night of glamping in permanent traditional tents, a short camel ride into the dunes. Dinner, drumming, more stars than you knew existed, and a sunrise you won't want to sleep through.

faqs.q: What's the castaway night on the Philippines trips?
faqs.a: One night on Daracotan Island in open-air beach bungalows with mosquito nets. A village visit, a cooking class, snorkelling over a shipwreck and a bonfire on the sand. No Wi-Fi, no need for it.
faqs.applies: Philippines West / Island Hopper / Total Philippines

faqs.q: Is food included?
faqs.a: Some of it. Welcome and farewell dinners are on every trip, along with the group feasts you'd never want to miss (family-style on a beach, the hill-tribe homestay). Most breakfasts are in too. We don't lock you into every meal, because you'll want to roam the street markets and find your own spots.

faqs.q: How many meals are included on my trip?
faqs.a: It's under 'What you get' on every trip page. Thailand Island Hopper, for example, includes 4 breakfasts, 4 lunches and 1 dinner; Morocco Uncovered 7 breakfasts, 1 lunch and 5 dinners.

faqs.q: Can dietary requirements be catered for?
faqs.a: Yes. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, halal and allergies are all fine if you tell us when you book, so your Local Legend and the places we eat can plan ahead.

faqs.q: Is there any free time?
faqs.a: Yes. Itineraries balance the moments we've planned with time to explore, shop, get a massage or do absolutely nothing. Your Local Legend will have first-hand recommendations for the free days.

faqs.q: What if I don't want to do an activity?
faqs.a: Then don't. Every activity is optional and there's never any pressure. Not feeling the open water? Stay on the boat. It's your trip.

faqs.q: Are there optional extras I'll be asked to pay for?
faqs.a: Everything on the itinerary is included: no bolt-ons, no tier menus. Some destinations have optional add-ons on free days (a dive, a scooter, rafting) that you can choose to do, but they're never required.

faqs.q: What happens in the evenings?
faqs.a: The group heads out for dinner most nights at places we've found over the years, and often on somewhere afterwards: a rooftop, a beach bar, a night market, a sunset. Evenings aren't on the itinerary and aren't compulsory, and there's always a non-drinking option. The best conversations tend to happen here.

faqs.q: Can I skip part of the trip to visit family and rejoin later?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The itinerary is fixed so the group stays together, but leaving and rejoining can work on some routes. Send us the exact dates and stops you're thinking of and we'll check with the ops team.

faqs.q: Can I customise the itinerary?
faqs.a: The group itinerary is fixed so everyone shares the same experience, but you can add pre- or post-nights, a private room and, on some trips, an extension like Komodo. Your Local Legend will also help you make the free time yours.

faqs.q: What's the language situation?
faqs.a: English gets you by in tourist areas everywhere we go, and your Local Legend handles the rest. A few local words always land well; by day two on the Vietnam trip you'll be ordering bún chả like a local.

faqs.q: Is it safe?
faqs.a: Every destination we run trips in is considered safe for travellers, and a small group with a Local Legend who knows the ground is the safest way to see them. Normal sense applies: watch your bag in busy markets and mind the traffic in Vietnam and India.

faqs.q: Do I need to dress a certain way?
faqs.a: In Morocco, India and Sri Lanka, and at temples anywhere in Asia, cover shoulders and knees. A light scarf or sarong does the job. Your Local Legend will give you a heads-up before temple days.
faqs.applies: Morocco / India / Sri Lanka / temple visits

faqs.q: How do you look after the places we visit?
faqs.a: Through our People & Planet Promise: 1% of revenue goes to people and planet initiatives, we measure and offset our carbon every month, and we build trips around community tourism enterprises, locally owned businesses like The Art House in Marrakech, the Bang Lamphu community in Bangkok and Horses of Gili. Leave a place better than you found it.

faqs.q: What's the People & Planet Promise?
faqs.a: Three measurable promises: positively impact 250,000 lives by 2030, generate £1.25 million for people and planet initiatives by 2030 (1% of our revenue, built into the business model, not donated after profit), and be climate positive now under the Glasgow Declaration. So far: 332,482 trees planted, £320,123 donated to 29 initiatives in 12 countries, 8,903 tonnes of carbon offset.

faqs.q: Which projects do you support?
faqs.a: Long-term partners, not one-off PR moments: charity: water (eight wells in rural Cambodia), Bali Street Mums, the Indigenous Literacy Foundation, Sungai Watch (river trash barriers in Bali) and Children of Vietnam (64 scholarships). Plus Planeterra projects on the ground, like our elephant sanctuary partner in Thailand.

faqs.q: How do I get from the airport to the start hotel?
faqs.a: Your arrival-day pickup is included: send us your flight details and a driver meets you at arrivals. Your Local Legend shares the hotel details in the WhatsApp group about a week before.

faqs.q: What if my flight is delayed and I miss the welcome dinner?
faqs.a: Don't panic. Message your Local Legend in the WhatsApp group with your new arrival time. Nothing happens before the welcome dinner on day 1, and they'll make sure you're settled and caught up.

faqs.q: How does the border crossing work on Cambodia & Vietnam Explorer?
faqs.a: By land at Moc Bai, with the group and your Local Legend. Have your Vietnam e-visa sorted before the trip and keep your passport handy.

faqs.q: Is there Wi-Fi on the Komodo liveaboard?
faqs.a: No, and that's the point. Three days of sunsets, stargazing and snorkelling with manta rays. Phone away.

faqs.q: What's Moyo Island?
faqs.a: A Tru-ly Unique day on the Komodo and Bali & Beyond trips: an island that only lets in around 50 visitors a day, with untouched waterfalls, clear water and a bike ride with local guides.

faqs.q: What is Bottle Beach?
faqs.a: A beach on Koh Phangan you can only reach by boat, and for one night it's ours. Volleyball, the viewpoint hike, dinner on the sand, cocktails and a private fire show. It's the kind of night that becomes a story before it's even over.

faqs.q: Can I pay a deposit?
faqs.a: Yes. Lock in your spot with £200 per person per trip (EUR 240, AUD 250, CAD 360, NZD 400, USD 280) and pay the rest by 60 days before departure. Booking within 60 days of departure? That's paid in full.

faqs.q: Is my spot guaranteed once I've paid a deposit?
faqs.a: Yes. The moment the deposit lands, the place is yours, as long as the balance clears 60 days before you go.

faqs.q: Is the deposit refundable?
faqs.a: It's non-refundable, but it is flexible: with 60+ days' notice you can move it to another date or trip (one free change) or transfer it to a friend.

faqs.q: Can I pay in instalments?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay your way: set up an automatic payment plan, make flexible payments whenever you like through your account (sign in with the email you booked with), use the link in your confirmation email, or call the team on +44 203 542 2463. Interest-free, as long as it's all paid 60 days before departure.

faqs.q: When is my final balance due?
faqs.a: 60 days before your trip starts. Pay it off in chunks or all at once through your account.

faqs.q: How do I book?
faqs.a: Hit Check Dates on any trip page, pick your departure and pay online with a debit or credit card. Or call the UK office on +44 203 542 2463 and a human will sort it.

faqs.q: Can I pay in my own currency?
faqs.a: Prices are shown and charged in GBP, AUD, CAD, EUR and USD. Any debit or credit card works; your bank converts at its own rate.

faqs.q: Why does the trip show a price per day?
faqs.a: So you can compare trips fairly. A 27-day trip costs more than an 8-day one, but per day it's often better value. The 'from' price is the lowest current departure; each date shows its own price and any saving.

faqs.q: My card was declined at checkout. What do I do?
faqs.a: International payments sometimes trigger a security check with banks outside the UK and EU. Give your bank a heads-up, try another card or PayPal, or ask us and we'll send a custom payment link to lock in your deposit.

faqs.q: My discount code isn't working.
faqs.a: Codes can be expired, mistyped or limited to full-price trips (most can't stack on sale prices). Send us the code and we'll check its rules.

faqs.q: Do prices ever change after I've booked?
faqs.a: Your price is fixed once the deposit is paid, apart from changes in fuel, taxes or exchange rates. We absorb increases up to 2%; anything above that is passed on, and if it ever exceeded 8% you could cancel for a full refund.

faqs.q: Can I change my trip date?
faqs.a: Yes. With 60+ days' notice you get one free date change to any available departure (or a trip of equal or higher value). Inside 60 days an admin fee applies and it's subject to availability; inside 30 days changes can't be guaranteed. No changes within 7 days of departure.

faqs.q: What does a change cost after the free one?
faqs.a: £50 per person per change (€65, US$70, AU$100), plus any costs from suppliers.

faqs.q: Can I transfer my booking or deposit to a friend?
faqs.a: Yes, up to 60 days before departure. Send us your booking reference and their details. A transfer fee of up to £100 per person may apply, plus any supplier costs.

faqs.q: What if I need to cancel?
faqs.a: More than 60 days before departure, you lose the deposit only. 60 days or less, the cancellation charge is 100% of the trip cost, which is exactly why insurance with cancellation cover matters. Insurance premiums and amendment fees aren't refundable.

faqs.q: Can I switch to a different trip?
faqs.a: Yes. With 60+ days' notice your deposit moves to any other trip or date for free (one change). Any price difference is payable, and credit stays on your account for next time.

faqs.q: What if TruTravels changes or cancels my trip?
faqs.a: Departures are guaranteed, so this is rare. If we ever had to make a significant change to an essential part of your package, you'd be offered an alternative or a full refund under the Package Travel Regulations.

faqs.q: How do multi-trip bundles work for payment?
faqs.a: Bundle two or more trips for 5% off. Each trip needs its £200 deposit, the full amount is due 60 days before the first trip starts, and all trips need to happen within 12 months of that first start date.

faqs.q: Can I use my VIP discount or travel credit on a sale price?
faqs.a: VIP discounts apply to full-price trips only. Travel credit can go on any booking, including sale trips.

faqs.q: When do I get my VIP travel credit?
faqs.a: At the start of each calendar year, based on your tier, straight into your account for any future booking.

faqs.q: Do my VIP days ever expire?
faqs.a: Never. Days are yours for life and you're never downgraded. Every day on every trip counts, multi-country included.

faqs.q: How do I manage my booking?
faqs.a: Log in to your account with the email you booked with. Bookings, saved trips, payments, transfers, passport and flight details and your VIP progress all live there.

faqs.q: I've forgotten my password.
faqs.a: Use the forgotten-password link on the login page and we'll email a reset. Make sure it's the email you booked with.

faqs.q: What time does the trip finish?
faqs.a: The last day is checkout day and the trip officially ends then. No activities, so treat it as a travel day. Late flight? Your Local Legend will have ideas for filling it, and there'll be details to swap and goodbyes to drag out.

faqs.q: Is transport to the airport included at the end?
faqs.a: Not as standard (Icons and above get it free). Your Local Legend can help you book a transfer or point you to the easiest option.

faqs.q: Can I book extra nights at the end?
faqs.a: Yes. We can arrange post-nights at the end hotel so you don't have to move. Send us the dates and we'll send rates. If you'd rather book yourself, we'll tell you the end hotel in advance so you can book the same place.

faqs.q: Can you help with onward travel?
faqs.a: That's what your Local Legend is there for. Another Tru trip, a few days on a beach, or the flight home: they'll point you in the right direction.

faqs.q: How do I get back to Bangkok from Koh Phangan after a Thailand trip?
faqs.a: Ferry to the mainland then bus or train to Bangkok (roughly 12 hours), or a short flight from Koh Samui, about 45 minutes away by ferry. Your Local Legend will help you book whichever suits.

faqs.q: The Thailand Island Hopper ends in Phuket. Can I fly home from there?
faqs.a: Yes. Phuket (HKT) is an international airport with plenty of connections, or fly to Bangkok. There's a ferry-and-bus option back to Bangkok too if you'd rather go overland.

faqs.q: How do I get back to Manila after Philippines West?
faqs.a: The trip ends in Coron. Coron's airport is about 30 minutes away with flights to Manila and Cebu. Book it yourself (it's not included), and early for the best fares.

faqs.q: How do I get home after the Philippines Island Hopper?
faqs.a: It ends on Boracay. Fly from Caticlan (MPH) to Manila, sometimes via Cebu, to connect with your international flight. That flight isn't included.

faqs.q: How do I get back from Labuan Bajo after the Komodo trip?
faqs.a: Labuan Bajo has an airport with short flights to Bali (Denpasar) and Lombok. Not included, and cheap if you book early.

faqs.q: How do I get to Colombo airport after Sri Lanka Uncovered?
faqs.a: The trip ends in Unawatuna, two to three hours by taxi from Colombo airport. Your Local Legend can arrange it.

faqs.q: Which airport do I fly out of at the end?
faqs.a: The end city on your trip page. For example: Bali Experience ends on Gili T (fly from Lombok or head back to Denpasar); Greece ends in Santorini (JTR); Legend of Japan in Osaka (KIX); Colombia in Cartagena (CTG); Brazil Experience in São Paulo (GRU); Vietnam Explorer in Hanoi. Morocco, Peru and India end where they start.

faqs.q: How much time should I leave between two back-to-back trips?
faqs.a: At least a day or two. That covers the flight between end and start cities and any visa admin, like the Vietnam e-visa after Thailand.

faqs.q: How do I share my photos and videos?
faqs.a: Upload them on the Share Your Photos page: JPG, PNG, HEIC, MP4 or MOV, up to 25 files at 200MB each, straight off your phone, unfiltered. Faces, not just views. Everyone who uploads goes into a quarterly draw for £250 travel credit. We may feature them on the site, social and emails (tagging you where we can), we never sell or pass them on, and you can ask us to take them down any time at hello@trutravels.com.

faqs.q: How do I leave a review?
faqs.a: Google, Trustpilot or TourRadar, whichever you use. We read every one, and the good bits end up on trip pages. Honest is better than glowing.

faqs.q: What are Stories?
faqs.a: Real moments from the road: video diaries from travellers, creators and Local Legends, plus long reads on destinations, first-timer tips, food, solo travel and more. Filter by destination or life moment. Got one? Upload it and it might end up there.

faqs.q: Does the community carry on after the trip?
faqs.a: That's usually the bit that lasts. The group chat keeps going, people meet up (there was a Tru Crew reunion in Lisbon: 14 countries, 23 humans, one rooftop), Legends get invited to an annual meetup and MVPs get their own events. Join the TruTravellers Facebook group and follow us on socials to stay in the loop.

faqs.q: Do I get anything for travelling with you again?
faqs.a: Every day on a trip counts towards your VIP status, for life. From 30 days you're a Game-Changer with 5% off full-price trips, travel credit each year and early access to sales, and it climbs from there. Check your progress on your dashboard; we'll email you when you level up.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own community on a trip, or earn from recommending you?
faqs.a: Yes to both. Host A Trip lets you run a Tru trip for your community, with us handling everything and you earning commission. Tru Affiliates gives you trackable links and commission on every booking you send our way. Both start with a short application on the Partners page.

faqs.q: Could I become a Local Legend?
faqs.a: Maybe. We hire people we'd happily spend fourteen days on a minibus with. Roles come up on the Join The Crew page, and you can send a speculative application to recruitment@trutravels.com with your CV, a short intro and what excites you about it.

faqs.q: I've got feedback or a problem after my trip. Who do I contact?
faqs.a: Email info@trutravels.com or call +44 203 542 2463 and a human will pick it up. Live chat runs 9:30am to 5pm GMT, Monday to Saturday.

voice.detail: Leave Ordinary Behind. Not escaping your life, expanding it. The destination is the setting; what happens to the person is the story.
Emotion creates desire, product removes uncertainty. In an FAQ the practical answer comes fast, but the framing is human: a real moment, a real person, then the reassurance and the next step.
Human, optimistic, social, adventurous, inclusive, alive. Confident without corporate, playful without trying too hard, emotional without sentimental. Talk like people who have actually travelled.
A Tru trip is a shared experience with an itinerary underneath it. 'Tour' only survives inside proper nouns (Explorer Tour URLs) and third-party names (TourRadar).
Never a cosmetic rename. Describe what they unlock: local perspective, human connection, confidence, moments no itinerary can script. 'More a mate who happens to know the way.'
Explain why the experience feels special rather than shouting 'exclusive'. Not scarcity for its own sake.
Local Lens · Rise Up · Bucket List · Tru-ly Unique · Unplugged. Tag only where the trip genuinely delivers it. The Social Layer (connection) is embedded, never a category.
When talking to guests about the change, it's an evolution of how we design and talk about trips, not a rebrand.
People. Together. Stories. Feel. Try. Discover. Local. Belong. Connect. Say yes. Your people. First time. Remember. Imagine. Present. Unexpected. Brave. Curious. Community. Extraordinary.

USP. Exclusive. Authentic. Best. Ultimate. Epic. Unforgettable. Bucket-list as a generic adjective. Life-changing without evidence. Hidden gem. Off the beaten track. Once-in-a-lifetime for ordinary activities. 'We take care of everything' as the whole pitch. Also drop 'maximise adventure, minimise hassle'-style product statements.
Don't say 'great group atmosphere'. Show it: solo arrivals becoming airport mates, a group chat that won't shut up, the Lisbon reunion. TruFam is earned through behaviour.
Curious, human, conversational. Ask open questions, match the customer's energy, never paste a brochure. Sales flow: Person → Possibility → Experience → Proof → Invitation.
Does it make someone feel something? Are people in it? Is a real moment visible? Have we earned any claim? Does it help someone Leave Ordinary Behind, or did we just put the words on the end?

No departure dates, availability, prices, sale percentages, hotel names, meeting or pick-up times, shuttle windows, transport fares or tipping amounts in answers. Point to the trip page or the Local Legend instead.
